newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Suncorp sees reduced 96/97 profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Suncorp sees reduced 96/97 profit.

text.p: Queensland state government owned Suncorp Insurance and Finance said on Monday that it expected lower profits in the year ended June 30, 1997.
"We expect to see reduced profits in 1996/97 due to falling investment returns, loss of margin and share in the home lending market," chief executive Bernard Rowley told a news conference.

Rowley declined to specify by how much profits might fall in the current year but said it was possible a reduction of "about A$60 million" could occur in total funds available for investment in the current year.

This was mainly because of earlier-reported provisions taken to the 1995/96 profit-and-loss account for long-term insurance claims liabilities and investment fluctuations required ahead of the planned merger with Metway Bank Ltd and Queensland Industry Development Corporation (QIDC), Rowley said.
New entrants in the financial services market were now "cherry picking with highly-focused strategies," Rowley said.
"Suncorp is fighting on a number of fronts against new mortgage entrants, new entrants into the general insurance market and new players in life insurance and superannuation," he said.

Both Rowley and Suncorp chairman Graham Tucker declined to comment on the planned merger that will create a new financial services with assets of A$19 billion and annual profits of more than A$200 million.
